bib.title: Open Problems in Applied Deep Learning

read.skipped: Reference list (offset 53659 onward) skimmed only for lineage.

question: What open problems arise when the model-iteration step of machine learning (hyper-parameter, architecture and data-augmentation search) is formulated as a bi-level optimization and extended from supervised learning to other learning settings?
hypothesis: Automating the iteration step (AutoML), which has shown promise on image classification, may not carry over to harder settings; the paper says this remains to be tested.
contributions: Formulates the ML mechanism as a bi-level optimization: an inner training loop and an outer iteration loop over hyper-parameters (Eq. 1).
Surveys, task by task from supervised to physics-informed learning, which performance metrics and design spaces make the iteration step an open problem.

results.claim: Hyper-parameter and architecture search by RL or evolution is very expensive, costing tens of thousands of GPU-hours.
results.source: Pham et al. 2018 [34]; Liu et al. 2018 [35] (as cited)
results.setup: Neural architecture search for image classification; the paper equates this to 450 GPUs for 3-4 days.
results.quote:
32,400-43,200
GPU-Hours, the equivalent of using 450 GPUs for 3-4 days

results.claim: Parameter sharing (warm-starting from shared weights held in memory) can cut the cost of solving Eq. 1 by up to 1000x.
results.setup: Parameter sharing trades computation for memory; 'in some cases', about 16 GPU-hours.
results.quote:
This could result in up to 1000x faster solutions to Eq. 1
(e.g., 16 GPU-Hours) in some cases.
results.note: Source page 4-5 line break; the 16 GPU-hours figure is given as an example, not as a measured baseline comparison.

results.claim: The iteration step (steps 1-4 repeated) is described as the most time- and resource-consuming part of the ML pipeline and is often overlooked.
results.setup: General statement about building ML solutions; steps 1-4 'repeated tens of thousands of times'. No data given.
results.quote:
The iteration step is a crucial piece
of the machine learning pipeline and is usually the most time and resource
consuming step while often being overlooked.

results.claim: The paper frames ML as a bi-level optimization: inner loop minimizes training loss over weights w, outer loop optimizes validation metric over hyper-parameters alpha.
results.setup: Eq. 1: min_alpha M_val(w*(alpha), alpha) s.t. w*(alpha)=argmin_w L_train(w, alpha).
results.quote:
The inner level optimization loop entails minimizing a
properly chosen loss function evaluated on the training data.

results.claim: AutoML has shown promise on simple supervised problems such as image classification, but success on harder problems is untested.
results.setup: Concluding remark; no experiments in the paper.
results.quote: It remains to be seen and tested in practice.

limits: Position paper: no experiments, datasets or measurements of its own; all numbers are cited from other work.
Scope is the training/iteration step (step 5 of 7); serving, monitoring and retraining get one sentence in the introduction and are not analysed.
Proposed directions (differentiable metric proxies, uncertainty-weighted multi-objective losses, human-in-the-loop RL) are suggestions, untested here.
Dated: written January 2023, before most LLM-era evaluation, RLHF and LLMOps practice; mentions ChatGPT only in passing.
practices: Treat the ML workflow as 7 steps: data as 'source code', model, training, validation, iteration, test, then serving with constant monitoring and retraining (Sec. 1, Fig. 1).
Use experiment tracking, dataset versioning and model management (e.g. Weights & Biases) to support the manual iteration process (Sec. 2).
Keep the data split to train, validation and test; avoid fragmenting data further to tune hyper-hyper-parameters (Sec. 3.1).

Choose the performance metric for the iteration loop deliberately: accuracy is discrete and non-differentiable, and metrics are ill-defined for unsupervised, generative and physics-informed settings (Sec. 2-3).
When one metric is insufficient, combine several (accuracy plus FLOPs, latency, memory) as a weighted multi-objective, but the weights are an open problem (Sec. 3.1).
Reduce the computational cost of iteration to reduce carbon footprint (Sec. 1).

terms.definition: the outer level optimization loop that maximizes a performance metric on validation data to pursue optimal model hyper-parameters, including model engineering, experiment tracking, dataset versioning and augmentation
additional hyper-parameters, such as objective weights, introduced for the outer optimization problem
Automatic Machine Learning: automating the iteration process rather than leaving it to practitioner intuition
